data_output.description: data.load returns the existing split dictionaries with canonical source-row order. Each loaded row retains its existing positional structure, except feature position row[4] is hour_bin in 0..5 rather than raw hour. data.encode returns (encoded, dimension), where encoded[split] is (features, labels, users); features is an int32 array of shape (row_count, 5) with globally offset, train-vocabulary categorical IDs in the order user_id, video_id, tab, hour_bin, weekday. Every field, including hour_bin, has one train-fitted unknown bucket.

model_input.description: Model receives the unchanged five-column encoded categorical matrix. Column 3 (zero-based) is the train-fitted six-bin hour_bin categorical ID instead of the former train-fitted 24-category hour ID. No model architecture, loss, sampling, optimizer, regularization, checkpoint rule, or configuration value changes.

feature_engineer.objective: Implement the hour-coarsening representation ablation exclusively in data.py: replace the existing categorical hour feature with a six-category four-hour bin derived from hourmin, while retaining the five-column additive feature interface.
required_changes: In data.py, change FIELDS from ["user_id", "video_id", "tab", "hour", "weekday"] to ["user_id", "video_id", "tab", "hour_bin", "weekday"].
Continue deriving integer hour from the exact raw log column row["hourmin"] with the canonical recipe hour = floor(numeric hourmin / 100), and retain the existing validation that hour is in 0..23.
Derive hour_bin as integer floor(hour / 4), yielding exactly values 0 through 5 for valid hours 0 through 23.
Store hour_bin, rather than raw hour, in each loaded row at the existing fourth feature position, so the row tuple remains compatible with the current positional accesses in encode().

Update encode()'s raw(row) function to return [row[1], row[2], row[3], row[4], row[5]], where row[4] is now the derived hour_bin. Do not add a sixth feature column or alter encode()'s returned tuple interface.

Fit the hour_bin vocabulary only by iterating training rows exactly as the existing vocabulary loop does. Preserve the existing one-unknown-ID-per-field behavior, including an unknown bucket for hour_bin in validation and test.
Do not read any source other than the existing standard log files and do not add raw fields, labels, aggregates, joins, or profile features.
preserve: Keep split date boundaries, source-file iteration order, selected-row order, label masking for test when include_test_labels is false, weekday derivation from the exact raw date column, and the user_id/video_id/tab/weekday categorical fields unchanged.

Keep encode() output as encoded[name] = (features, labels, users), with features dtype int32, exactly five feature columns, train-fitted per-field vocabularies, per-field unknown buckets, and offsets.
Do not modify model.py, train.py, or config.json. The existing model requirement for five feature columns must remain satisfied without changes.
Do not use test labels for fitting any representation or vocabulary.
coordination_notes: The shared data-to-model contract remains a two-dimensional int32 feature matrix with five globally offset categorical IDs per row in this exact order: user_id, video_id, tab, hour_bin, weekday.
hour_bin is derived solely from raw hourmin via hour = floor(float(hourmin) / 100), then hour_bin = floor(hour / 4); no source-column alias is permitted.
Trainer-owned train.py will continue to emit predictions_valid.npz and predictions_test.npz in encoded validation and test row order, respectively, so preserve source row ordering exactly.

reasoning: The hypothesis is a single feature-representation ablation. Only data.py requires modification because the additive model already consumes five categorical columns and train.py/config.json already preserve the requested optimizer, K=4 uniform same-user negative sampling, pairwise loss, validation-only checkpoint selection, and canonical prediction archive behavior. The six-bin category is derived from the schema-approved raw hourmin field using the canonical hour derivation followed by the requested floor(hour/4) transformation; vocabularies remain train-fitted with the existing unknown bucket.
